findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the decision rule for an empty changed-files review under the new `["**"]` spelling (define whether repository-wide selects unconditionally like the prior `[]` ungated path), and add a contract-test case covering empty changed_files so AC4's 'membership unchanged' claim is actually proven at the diverging edge.
evidence: `criteria/overlay.py::_validate_applies_to` docstring: 'an empty glob list means UNGATED for a project criterion ... An empty LIST stays legal: that is the deliberate "ungated" spelling this repo's own overlay uses.'

`code_review/registry.py::project_criterion_applies` L340-343: `globs = project_applies_to_globs(...); if not globs: return True; return any(_glob_match(f, g) for f in changed_files for g in globs)` — `["**"]` takes the glob branch, `[]` takes the unconditional-True branch.

`_engine_support/commit_impact.py::glob_match` L36-43 is fnmatch-based; `any(...)` over an empty `changed_files` is False, so `["**"]` selects nothing when no files changed while `[]` selected the criterion.
`workflow/gate_dispatch.py` L432: `_activated_code_review_project_criteria(repo_root, changed_files: Sequence[str] = ())` — empty changed_files is a representable state at this seam.
ADR 0074 L94-101 confirms project `applies_to: []` means 'runs on every review'.
findings.finding: The migration of `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `applies_to: []` to `["**"]` changes the selection code path from the ungated short-circuit (`if not globs: return True`) to glob-matching over changed files, which diverges on an empty changed-files review — so the AC claim that review membership is 'unchanged by the migration' is not universally true and the empty-changed-files fallback is unspecified.
findings.location: Approach ('Migrate `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` entry ... from `[]` to `["**"]`') and Acceptance Criteria bullet 4
scenarios: A code-review invocation whose resolved changed-files list is empty (e.g. metadata-only or no-diff review) where `project.review-phase-boundaries` currently runs under `[]` but would be recorded non-applicable under `["**"]`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) define `["**"]` selection as short-circuiting True when `changed_files` is empty (matching the prior ungated semantics) and state this in the Approach, or (b) explicitly document the intended behavior change for empty-diff reviews and add a negative-control test asserting it — do not leave the empty-changed-files fallback implicit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify WHERE the gate-specific project-code-review-LLM applies_to rule (empty→error, ["**"]→repo-wide) is enforced so it does not regress the SHARED criteria/overlay._validate_applies_to (which legally permits [] today) nor plan-review project criteria, and still fails at load/compile before any model call.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:190-210 _validate_applies_to: 'An empty LIST stays legal: that is the deliberate "ungated" spelling this repo's own overlay uses' — a SHARED validator across plan_review and code_review
docs/adr/0074 row: a `project.<name>` criterion is 'ungated — runs on every review'; 'one that wants to run always states []'

Plan makes empty applies_to an ERROR for project code-review LLM criteria and requires ["**"], but does not scope this away from the shared validator or plan-review project criteria (which carry no applies_to)
findings.finding: The plan's new gate-specific applies_to rule (empty/missing/non-list/blank fails; ["**"] = repository-wide) conflicts with the CURRENTLY-SHARED validator _validate_applies_to in criteria/overlay.py, which is called for BOTH gates and deliberately permits an empty list as the 'ungated' spelling; the plan does not say where the new stricter, code-review-project-LLM-only validation lives so as not to regress plan-review project criteria or the shared load-time contract.
findings.location: Approach — 'Keep applicability vocabularies gate-specific... validate applies_to as a non-empty list...'
scenarios: A plan-review project criterion or a built-in re-tune passes through the same load-time validator and either newly errors or the new rule silently does not apply where intended
The stricter rule is added to the shared _validate_applies_to and breaks the existing legal empty-list contract for plan-review
findings.suggested_fix: State that the stricter non-empty-glob + ["**"] rule is applied only to `code_review` `project.` criteria at snapshot-compile (or a code-review-gated hook), leaving the shared `_validate_applies_to` empty-list contract intact for plan-review, and note the migration of `project.review-phase-boundaries` [] → ["**"] is what keeps THIS repo's overlay legal under the new rule.

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Approach and the ADR, cite and distinguish the relevant in-repo prior art — ADR 0098's immutable/fingerprinted `OperationSnapshot`, ADR 0017's unified-registry delegation, and `overlay.py`'s existing content-digest + per-signature memoized effective view — and justify why a new `CriteriaSnapshot` authority (with its own digest) is preferable to composing beside/within those, or reusing the overlay signature.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'Create a repository-bound CriteriaSnapshot… compiles effective built-ins… and one deterministic digest… Consumers receive the snapshot; they do not reread ambient policy.'

ADR 0098 §1: 'Every operation resolves one immutable, serializable, non-secret OperationSnapshot… An in-progress operation never rereads environment, configuration files, cwd… an existing snapshot is never mutated or partly reloaded' — an existing immutable digest/fingerprinted policy authority the plan re-derives without citing.

ADR 0017 §Decision: the plan extends the very layer this ADR created ('one shared rebar.llm.criteria layer'), and its 'DELEGATION, not rip-and-replace' / byte-identical-for-overlay-absent posture mirrors the plan's compatibility-adapter + golden-contract approach — uncredited.

src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:154-165 `_overlay_signature` computes a sha256 content digest; `_effective_routing_cached` (lines 333-369) is an immutable, per-(gate,repo,signature) memoized effective view — the plan's 'immutable digest-bound view' partly exists already.

ADR bullet lists what to document but not the prior-art comparison: 'why a single effective authority is preferable to gate-specific registry reads' — asserted, not grounded against ADR 0098 / 0017 / the existing memoization.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel immutable, digest-bound single-authority `CriteriaSnapshot` and mandates an ADR, but neither the Approach nor the ADR bullet considers the repo's directly relevant prior art — ADR 0098's immutable/fingerprinted `OperationSnapshot` policy authority, ADR 0017's unified-criteria-registry delegation model, and the existing `overlay.py` content-digest + per-signature memoized effective view — so the new authority is chosen with no anti-repackaging justification.
findings.location: Approach section ("Create a repository-bound CriteriaSnapshot… one deterministic digest") and the ADR bullet ("why a single effective authority is preferable to gate-specific registry reads")
scenarios: Reviewers/authors cannot tell whether `CriteriaSnapshot` should be a new type or a projection composed beside/within the ADR 0098 OperationSnapshot.
The new digest may duplicate the overlay content-signature already used for cache isolation, creating two competing 'authoritative' digests.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Alternatives / prior art' paragraph to the Approach and a matching ADR section: state whether `CriteriaSnapshot` is a projection composed with (not duplicating) the ADR 0098 OperationSnapshot, whether its deterministic digest reuses or extends the existing `_overlay_signature`, and why gate-specific registry reads (post-ADR 0017 delegation) cannot be tightened in place — grounding the 'single authority is preferable' claim in these precedents rather than asserting it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the digest computation protocol in the plan body: the exact ordered set of inputs (effective built-ins, project LLM/DET criteria, routing/posture/applicability metadata, source locations), the canonical serialization/ordering, and the hash function.
evidence: 'compiles ... one deterministic digest from the provided repository root and already-resolved operation inputs'
AC1: 'yields one immutable digest-bound view'
AC6: 'An ADR documents ... digest inputs'
A derived value (digest) with no stated computation/aggregation protocol is an ordinary data-design ambiguity under E2 signal (2)
findings.finding: The 'deterministic digest' has no stated computation protocol (which fields are hashed, canonical ordering, and hash algorithm), yet tests assert 'digest behavior' and the AC requires 'one immutable digest-bound view'. The digest inputs are only deferred to the ADR (AC6), leaving the plan body under-specifying the derived value the executor must make deterministic.
findings.location: Approach ('one deterministic digest'); Acceptance Criteria 1 and 6
scenarios: Executor must implement a stable digest but has no stated field set / ordering, risking non-reproducible digests across runs or platforms
A 'digest behavior' test cannot be written to a fixed expected value without the canonical input list
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach naming the digest inputs and canonicalization, e.g. 'the digest is a SHA-256 over the canonically-sorted JSON of effective criteria ids, their retune/disable state, project DET entries, and applicability globs — excluding volatile source-path prefixes'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State positively why a new immutable digest-bound CriteriaSnapshot is preferable to simply routing the packaged-only code-review consumers (det_criteria/applies_to_globs/criterion_for_detector) through the EXISTING effective_routing()/effective_criteria() — e.g. the single-digest atomicity / one-view guarantee that separate effective reads cannot give.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:207 det_criteria() iterates routing_index() (packaged-only), not effective_routing()
src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:240 applies_to_globs() reads routing_index()
src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:174-187 effective_routing()/effective_criteria() already merge the overlay (disable/retune/project-add) via the shared core
Alternative: rewire det_criteria/applies_to_globs/criterion_for_detector to consult effective_routing(repo_root) — smaller blast radius, reuses tested cache-isolated merge
findings.finding: The plan introduces a whole new immutable CriteriaSnapshot authority, but the named defects (project DET disappears, project disable/retune ignored) are actually caused by three code-review consumers reading packaged-only routing_index() instead of the ALREADY-EXISTING effective_routing()/effective_criteria(); the plan does not weigh the cheaper alternative of routing those consumers through the existing effective view against building a new snapshot type.
findings.location: Context/Problem + Approach — 'code review then consults packaged-only overlay and detector registries' / 'Create a repository-bound CriteriaSnapshot'
scenarios: A reviewer/implementer asks why a new snapshot type is needed when the effective merge already exists and only three consumers bypass it
